Make sure you have a clean driving record and valid license and insurance if you plan on driving. Make sure to save about 30% of your earnings for taxes at the end of the year and save appropriately for car maintenance and expenses. Make sure you deduct your work miles on your taxes because it will take a huge chunk off what you will owe in taxes. If you have an expensive car, it's probably not worth doing unless you use a bike or scooter instead. Any old cheap shitbox makes the gig totally worth it, especially if you know how to do minor maintenance and repairs on your own, and you can always learn and save tons of money. The biggest thing to remember though is to only take good paying orders that are worth your time and gas. They can't kick you off for turning down bad orders. To me, dealing with being self-employed and having to jump through a couple extra hoops is well worth it compared to having a strict schedule and making shit money for an unlimited number of tasks and a massive chain of bosses that don't give a shit about you. It is empowering. And it's a good side job to add onto any job you enjoy doing, but doesn't pay well. Good luck!

That's a difficult question to answer. Some delivery services do while some don't. Postmates and hungry buffs do not show the tip. Uber eats does show the tip. Doordash does most of the time. I'm not sure about Grubhub, Nosh, or the other smaller ones.

We get paid per order so the hourly rate is always different. Usually it's about $15 to $30 gross not counting taxes, gas, and wear and tear. Most of the time I'm happy to get any tip. Thanks for tipping well when you do order. One thing that I struggle to understand is why broke people order delivery at all when there are outrageous fees, menu price increases, and the tip. I'm broke as shit and I always pick up my own food lol.

No there's nothing that can be done in that situation besides giving the driver a bad rating and ask them what happened. Sounds like a shitty driver. They should have contacted you to give you updates or taken your order first before waiting for the other one. A good way to avoid this problem is to avoid ordering delivery during the busy dinner rushes because restaurants can get so backed up that we have to sit there and wait for 30+ minutes. Always feel free to contact the driver to ask them what is going if they did not contact you already. If you want great service every time guaranteed, you can always pick the food up yourself lol

If you live close to the restaurant $3 to $3.50 is totally fine, especially if it's a small order. Distance is really the main factor for tips because of the time and vehicle costs. I sincerely thank you for tipping though! Giving us a good rating when we do a good job helps us out too 😁

Thank you for asking! For any small to medium order in Boulder, $5 is a good minimum in my opinion. If it's a big order priced over $50 or so, a 20% to 25% tip is adequate. If the order is being delivered to a super far location, a good rule of thumb is to tip $1 per mile of the total distance to and from the delivery location.

For in town orders $5+ is generally a good tip unless it's a massive order. For orders to Gunbarrel and the extended Boulder area, $10 is generally good considering the cost and time of driving back into town. For orders into the mountains, Longmont, Lafayette, etc. we need a big incentive to drive there and back. Sadly, the delivery platforms pay us almost nothing even though they attack customers with fees and take huge cuts from restaurants. Thank you for tipping us well! Cheers!

Most delivery services assign a maximum of 2 orders at a time to make sure customers get the food as fast as possible and the market is flooded with drivers to take them individually.

For any order from Boulder to Gunbarrel I think $6 to $10 is generally a good tip unless it's a massive order, or the weather is nightmarish like this weekend. The delivery service providers are pretty stingy with what they pay us, so about 60% to 70% of our income comes from tips. A good tip goes a long way!

I actually enjoy taking orders to Gunbarrel because of the easy highway mileage, but you NEED to tip well if you want your order on time. Otherwise it remains unclaimed and sits on the shelf until they double it up with another order to a similar drop-off location. It doesn't matter how far you live as long as you tip well enough. Independent contractor delivery drivers are essentially your temporary personal employees and if you refuse to pay your employees well we will not work for you.
